definitions.meaning: A green plant that makes its own food by photosynthesis and starts every food chain.
An animal that eats producers, such as a rabbit eating grass.
An animal that eats primary consumers, such as a fox eating a rabbit.
An organism that breaks down dead material and waste, returning nutrients to the soil.
A sequence showing who eats whom, and so the path energy takes through an ecosystem.
A diagram whose shrinking levels show that only about a tenth of the energy passes to the next level.
The loop by which carbon moves between air, living things, soil and fossil fuels.
The process by which plants absorb carbon dioxide and make food using sunlight.
The process by which living things release energy from food, returning carbon dioxide to the air.
A store or process that takes carbon dioxide out of the air, such as a growing forest.
Mineral substances that loop between soil and living things and are reused again and again.

mechanismSteps: Links form: grass the producer is eaten by the rabbit, the primary consumer, which the fox, the secondary consumer, eats - decomposers work on every link (s1).
Energy shrinks: only about a tenth passes to the next level, so the pyramid narrows and top carnivores stay few (s2).
Carbon loops: plants absorb carbon dioxide in photosynthesis while respiration and decomposition return it (s3).
Humans tip it: deforestation removes a sink and carbon dioxide piles up; replanting restores the sink (s4).
Flow versus loop: energy escapes as heat and never returns, while nutrients travel plant to animal to soil and back (s5).
objectives: Build a food chain and name producer, primary consumer, secondary consumer and decomposer
Explain why only about a tenth of the energy passes to the next level
Describe the carbon cycle and how deforestation and replanting tip it
subject: science
title: Ecology: food webs, energy flow, the carbon cycle

trap.explanation: The slip: The "cycle of life" language makes energy sound like something that loops round forever. The fix: Energy is not recycled: only about a tenth passes to the next level, the rest is lost as heat. In class, replay the myth scene: put the energy path and the nutrient path side by side and ask which one returns to its start - only the nutrient path does.
trap.misconception: Energy is recycled around the food chain like nutrients are.

workedExample: Test the recycling claim on the rabbit link. Step 1 (s2): the grass holds 100 units of energy and the rabbit gains only about 10. Step 2 (s5): the other 90 left as heat while the rabbit lived and moved. Heat cannot flow back into the grass, so the energy is gone from the chain - it was spent, not recycled.
